start.README.md:
# Router for a harbour fee service

This library decides which handler serves a request for a harbour fee service. `route(table, requests)` reads a *route table* and a list of requests and answers one line per request. There is no network: everything is text.

## Route table

One route per line: `PATTERN HANDLER` (exactly two words separated by blanks). Routes answer every request; requests carry no method.
Everything from `#` to the end of a line is a comment; lines without words are ignored. Lines are numbered from 1 (comments and blank lines count).

A **handler** is 1 to 24 characters: a lower-case ASCII letter, then lower-case letters, digits or `_`.

A **pattern** starts with `/`. The pattern `/` alone is the root. Otherwise it is segments separated by single `/`, with no empty segment and **no trailing slash**. A segment is:

* a *literal*: one or more of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -`;
* a *parameter* `:name`: matches any one non-empty path segment and captures it. `name` is 1 to 16 characters, a lower-case letter then lower-case letters, digits or `_`, and a name may occur only once in a pattern;

A line with the wrong number of words is `bad directive`; otherwise an invalid pattern `bad pattern`, an invalid handler `bad handler` (checked in that order). The first bad line makes the whole result `error: table line N: REASON`.

## Requests

Each non-blank line is just a `PATH` (exactly one word). Lines starting with `#` (after optional blanks) and blank lines produce no output. A request line that does not have the right shape gets the answer `400`.

The **path** is the word after the method with everything from the first `?` removed (the query string is ignored). It must start with `/`, otherwise `400`. The root path is `/`. For any other path the text after the first `/` is split at every `/` into segments. An empty segment *inside* the path (`//`) is `400`. A path with a trailing `/` ends with one empty segment: with the **strict** slash policy it stays, and since no pattern segment can match an empty segment `/a/` is just a path that matches nothing (`404` unless the 400 rules above apply); 

## Matching

A route's pattern **matches** a path if the path has exactly as many segments as the pattern (a wildcard takes all the rest, at least one), and every pattern segment accepts its path segment: literals must be equal (case-sensitively), parameters need a non-empty segment.

If several routes match, the best one wins: compare their patterns segment by segment from the left, ranking literal > parameter (a position that exists in only one pattern ranks below any kind); the first difference decides; if still tied the route written **first** wins.

## Answers

* `200 HANDLER name=value ...`: the winning route's handler followed by its captures in the order of the pattern (`name=value`, separated by single blanks; no captures, nothing more).
* `404`: no route's pattern matches the path.
* `400`: malformed request (see above).

The result is the answers joined by `\n` (no trailing newline); with no requests it is the empty text.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/router.js`:

```
function route(table, requests)  // returns a string; exported with module.exports
```

* `table`: the route table text
* `requests`: the requests, one per line
* returns one answer line per request (or an `error: table line ...` text).

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Table:

```
/ report
/ edit_item
/tags/:id search
/ create_item
```

Requests:

```
/tags/42
/
/
/
//
```

Answers:

```
200 search id=42
200 report
200 report
200 report
400
```

Table:

```
/v1/:slug create_item
/:rest health
/:slug report
/:slug/:id user
/:n/status/docs files
```

Requests:

```
/x_y
/x_y
/x_y/
/abc/status/docs
/x_y/extra
/x_y
```

Answers:

```
200 health rest=x_y
200 health rest=x_y
404
200 files n=abc
200 user slug=x_y id=extra
200 health rest=x_y
```

Table:

```
/:id show_item
/files/:n/status feed
/ docs
/files/:name/api files
```

Requests:

```
/Q
/Q
/files/abc/status?x=1&y=%20
/
/
```

Answers:

```
200 show_item id=Q
200 show_item id=Q
200 feed n=abc
200 docs
200 docs
```

start.README.md:
# Router for the tide-clock backend

This library decides which handler serves a request for the tide-clock backend. `route(table, requests)` reads a *route table* and a list of requests and answers one line per request. There is no network: everything is text.

## Route table

One route per line: `PATTERN HANDLER` (exactly two words separated by blanks). Routes answer every request; requests carry no method.
Everything from `#` to the end of a line is a comment; lines without words are ignored. Lines are numbered from 1 (comments and blank lines count).

A **handler** is 1 to 24 characters: a lower-case ASCII letter, then lower-case letters, digits or `_`.

A **pattern** starts with `/`. The pattern `/` alone is the root. Otherwise it is segments separated by single `/`, with no empty segment and **no trailing slash**. A segment is:

* a *literal*: one or more of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -`;
* a *parameter* `:name`: matches any one non-empty path segment and captures it. `name` is 1 to 16 characters, a lower-case letter then lower-case letters, digits or `_`, and a name may occur only once in a pattern;

A line with the wrong number of words is `bad directive`; otherwise an invalid pattern `bad pattern`, an invalid handler `bad handler` (checked in that order). The first bad line makes the whole result `error: table line N: REASON`.

## Requests

Each non-blank line is just a `PATH` (exactly one word). Lines starting with `#` (after optional blanks) and blank lines produce no output. A request line that does not have the right shape gets the answer `400`.

The **path** is the word after the method with everything from the first `?` removed (the query string is ignored). It must start with `/`, otherwise `400`. The root path is `/`. For any other path the text after the first `/` is split at every `/` into segments. An empty segment *inside* the path (`//`) is `400`. A path with a trailing `/` ends with one empty segment: with the **strict** slash policy it stays, and since no pattern segment can match an empty segment `/a/` is just a path that matches nothing (`404` unless the 400 rules above apply); 

## Matching

A route's pattern **matches** a path if the path has exactly as many segments as the pattern (a wildcard takes all the rest, at least one), and every pattern segment accepts its path segment: literals must be equal (case-sensitively), parameters need a non-empty segment.

If several routes match, the best one wins: compare their patterns segment by segment from the left, ranking literal > parameter (a position that exists in only one pattern ranks below any kind); the first difference decides; if still tied the route written **first** wins.

## Answers

* `200 HANDLER name=value ...`: the winning route's handler followed by its captures in the order of the pattern (`name=value`, separated by single blanks; no captures, nothing more).
* `404`: no route's pattern matches the path.
* `400`: malformed request (see above).

The result is the answers joined by `\n` (no trailing newline); with no requests it is the empty text.

## Interface

Implement this function in `router.go` (package `router`, module `example.com/router`):

```
func Route(table, requests string) string
```

* `table`: the route table text
* `requests`: the requests, one per line
* returns one answer line per request (or an `error: table line ...` text).

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Table:

```
/:n about
/files home
/:rest home
/:id/:key/v1 files
```

Requests:

```
/files/
/files
/Q/x_y/v1
/42/
/zzz/files
```

Answers:

```
404
200 home
200 files id=Q key=x_y
404
404
```

Table:

```
/:rest/:name feed
/ search
/:rest health
/orders/:key health
/items about
```

Requests:

```
/items
/
/orders/42/
/orders/42?x=1&y=%20
/
/orders/42
```

Answers:

```
200 about
200 search
404
200 health key=42
200 search
200 health key=42
```

Table:

```
/:slug home
/ user
/docs/:id/api health
/:slug docs
```

Requests:

```
/docs/abc/api
/abc
/abc?x=1&y=%20
/abc
/
```

Answers:

```
200 health id=abc
200 home slug=abc
200 home slug=abc
200 home slug=abc
200 user
```

# Router for the Saltmarsh library service

This library decides which handler serves a request for the Saltmarsh library service. `route(table, requests)` reads a *route table* and a list of requests and answers one line per request. There is no network: everything is text.

## Route table

One route per line: `METHOD PATTERN HANDLER` (exactly three words separated by blanks). `METHOD` is one of `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, or `*` (any method).
Everything from `#` to the end of a line is a comment; lines without words are ignored. Lines are numbered from 1 (comments and blank lines count).

A **handler** is 1 to 24 characters: a lower-case ASCII letter, then lower-case letters, digits or `_`.

A **pattern** starts with `/`. The pattern `/` alone is the root. Otherwise it is segments separated by single `/`, with no empty segment and **no trailing slash**. A segment is:

* a *literal*: one or more of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -`;
* a *parameter* `:name`: matches any one non-empty path segment and captures it; `:name<type>` matches only segments of that type, with the types `alpha`, `hex`, `slug`. `name` is 1 to 16 characters, a lower-case letter then lower-case letters, digits or `_`, and a name may occur only once in a pattern;
* the types: `alpha`: ASCII letters, either case; `hex`: ASCII hex digits, either case; `slug`: lower-case letters and digits in groups separated by single `-` (no leading, trailing or double `-`);

A line with the wrong number of words is `bad directive`; otherwise an unknown method is `bad method`, an invalid pattern `bad pattern`, an invalid handler `bad handler` (checked in that order). The first bad line makes the whole result `error: table line N: REASON`.

## Requests

Each non-blank line is `METHOD PATH` (exactly two words): the method is one or more upper-case ASCII letters (any such word is allowed, not only the six above). Lines starting with `#` (after optional blanks) and blank lines produce no output. A request line that does not have the right shape gets the answer `400`.

The **path** is the word after the method with everything from the first `?` removed (the query string is ignored). It must start with `/`, otherwise `400`. The root path is `/`. For any other path the text after the first `/` is split at every `/` into segments. An empty segment *inside* the path (`//`) is `400`. A path with a trailing `/` ends with one empty segment: with the **strict** slash policy it stays, and since no pattern segment can match an empty segment `/a/` is just a path that matches nothing (`404` unless the 400 rules above apply); 

## Matching

A route's pattern **matches** a path if the path has exactly as many segments as the pattern (a wildcard takes all the rest, at least one), and every pattern segment accepts its path segment: literals must be equal (case-sensitively), parameters need a non-empty segment of the right type.

A matching route is *eligible* when its method is `*`, equals the request method, or is `GET` while the request method is `HEAD`. If several routes are eligible, the best one wins: compare their patterns segment by segment from the left, ranking literal > typed parameter > parameter (a position that exists in only one pattern ranks below any kind); the first difference decides. If the patterns are equally specific, an exact method match beats `*`, which beats `GET`-for-`HEAD`; if still tied, the route written **first** in the table wins.

## Answers

* `200 HANDLER name=value ...`: the winning route's handler followed by its captures in the order of the pattern (`name=value`, separated by single blanks; no captures, nothing more).
* `405 allow=M1,M2,...`: no route is eligible but at least one route's pattern matches the path. The methods are collected from those routes (a `*` route contributes all six methods, a `GET` route contributes `GET` and `HEAD`), without duplicates, in the order `GET,HEAD,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE`.
* `404`: no route's pattern matches the path.
* `400`: malformed request (see above).

The result is the answers joined by `\n` (no trailing newline); with no requests it is the empty text.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/Router.java` (class `Router`, default package):

```
public static String route(String table, String requests)
```

* `table`: the route table text
* `requests`: the requests, one per line
* returns one answer line per request (or an `error: table line ...` text).

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

module Router
  HAS_METHODS = true
  TYPES = ['hex', 'int']
  HAS_WILD = false
  LENIENT = false
  CASEI = false
  HAS_PCT = false
  METHODS = %w[GET HEAD POST PUT PATCH DELETE]
  LOW = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'
  UP = LOW.upcase
  DG = '0123456789'
  HEX = '0123456789abcdefABCDEF'
  RANK = { 'lit' => 3, 'typed' => 2, 'param' => 1, 'wild' => 0 }

  def self.all?(s, set)
    s.each_char.all? { |c| set.include?(c) }
  end

  def self.ident?(s, max)
    s.length >= 1 && s.length <= max && LOW.include?(s[0]) && all?(s, LOW + DG + '_')
  end

  def self.parse_pattern(p)
    return [] if p == '/'
    return nil if !p.start_with?('/') || p.end_with?('/')
    segs = []
    names = []
    parts = p[1..].split('/', -1)
    parts.each_with_index do |s, i|
      return nil if s.empty?
      if s[0] == ':'
        body = s[1..]
        typ = nil
        if body.include?('<')
          return nil if !body.end_with?('>') || body.count('<') != 1
          inner = body[0...-1]
          body, typ = inner.split('<', 2)
          return nil unless TYPES.include?(typ)
        end
        return nil if !ident?(body, 16) || names.include?(body)
        names << body
        segs << [typ ? 'typed' : 'param', body, typ]
      elsif s[0] == '*'
        nm = s[1..]
        return nil if !HAS_WILD || i != parts.length - 1 || !ident?(nm, 16) || names.include?(nm)
        segs << ['wild', nm, nil]
      else
        return nil unless all?(s, LOW + UP + DG + '._~-')
        segs << ['lit', s, nil]
      end
    end
    segs
  end

  def self.type_ok?(typ, s)
    case typ
    when 'int' then s.length >= 1 && s.length <= 9 && all?(s, DG)
    when 'slug' then !s.empty? && all?(s, LOW + DG + '-') && !s.start_with?('-') && !s.end_with?('-') && !s.include?('--')
    when 'alpha' then !s.empty? && all?(s, LOW + UP)
    else !s.empty? && all?(s, HEX)
    end
  end

  def self.match(segs, path)
    caps = []
    i = 0
    segs.each do |kind, name, typ|
      if kind == 'wild'
        return nil if i >= path.length
        caps << [name, path[i..].join('/')]
        return caps
      end
      return nil if i >= path.length
      s = path[i]
      if kind == 'lit'
        return nil if (CASEI ? s.downcase != name.downcase : s != name)
      else
        return nil if s.empty?
        return nil if kind == 'typed' && !type_ok?(typ, s)
        caps << [name, s]
      end
      i += 1
    end
    i == path.length ? caps : nil
  end

  def self.decode(seg)
    out = +''
    i = 0
    while i < seg.length
      c = seg[i]
      if c == '%'
        h = seg[i + 1, 2]
        return nil if h.nil? || h.length != 2 || !all?(h, HEX)
        c = h.to_i(16).chr
        i += 3
      else
        i += 1
      end
      return nil if c < ' ' || c > '~'
      out << c
    end
    out
  end

  def self.parse_table(text)
    routes = []
    text.split("\n", -1).each_with_index do |raw, i|
      w = raw.split('#', 2)[0].to_s.split
      next if w.empty?
      pre = "error: table line #{i + 1}: "
      return [nil, pre + 'bad directive'] if w.length != (HAS_METHODS ? 3 : 2)
      method = '*'
      if HAS_METHODS
        method = w[0]
        return [nil, pre + 'bad method'] if method != '*' && !METHODS.include?(method)
      end
      segs = parse_pattern(w[-2])
      return [nil, pre + 'bad pattern'] if segs.nil?
      return [nil, pre + 'bad handler'] unless ident?(w[-1], 24)
      routes << [method, segs, w[-1]]
    end
    [routes, nil]
  end

  def self.route(table, requests)
    routes, err = parse_table(table)
    return err if err
    out = []
    requests.split("\n", -1).each do |raw|
      next if raw.sub(/\A[ \t]+/, '').start_with?('#')
      w = raw.split
      next if w.empty?
      if w.length != (HAS_METHODS ? 2 : 1)
        out << '400'
        next
      end
      method = 'GET'
      if HAS_METHODS
        method = w[0]
        unless method.match?(/\A[A-Z]+\z/)
          out << '400'
          next
        end
      end
      path = w[-1].split('?', 2)[0].to_s
      unless path.start_with?('/')
        out << '400'
        next
      end
      body = path[1..]
      if path == '/'
        segs = []
      else
        body = body[0...-1] if LENIENT && body.end_with?('/')
        segs = body.empty? ? [''] : body.split('/', -1)
        bad = segs.length == 1 && segs[0].empty? && body.empty?
        segs[0...-1].each { |s| bad = true if s.empty? }
        if bad
          out << '400'
          next
        end
      end
      if HAS_PCT
        dec = []
        bad = false
        segs.each do |s|
          d = decode(s)
          if d.nil?
            bad = true
            break
          end
          dec << d
        end
        if bad
          out << '400'
          next
        end
        segs = dec
      end
      best = nil
      pathmatch = []
      routes.each do |m, rs, h|
        caps = match(rs, segs)
        next if caps.nil?
        pathmatch << m
        next unless m == '*' || m == method || (method == 'HEAD' && m == 'GET')
        spec = rs.map { |k, _, _| RANK[k] }
        exact = m == method ? 2 : m == '*' ? 1 : 0
        if best.nil?
          best = [spec, exact, h, caps]
          next
        end
        n = [spec.length, best[0].length].max
        cmp = 0
        k = 0
        while k < n && cmp == 0
          a = k < spec.length ? spec[k] : -1
          b = k < best[0].length ? best[0][k] : -1
          cmp = a - b
          k += 1
        end
        cmp = exact - best[1] if cmp == 0
        best = [spec, exact, h, caps] if cmp > 0
      end
      if best
        out << (['200', best[2]] + best[3].map { |k, v| "#{k}=#{v}" }).join(' ')
      elsif !pathmatch.empty?
        allowed = []
        pathmatch.each do |m|
          if m == '*' then allowed.concat(METHODS)
          elsif m == 'GET' then allowed.push('GET', 'HEAD')
          else allowed << m
          end
        end
        out << ('405 allow=' + METHODS.select { |x| allowed.include?(x) }.join(','))
      else
        out << '404'
      end
    end
    out.join("\n")
  end
end

start.README.md:
# Router for the ferry booking API

This library decides which handler serves a request for the ferry booking API. `route(table, requests)` reads a *route table* and a list of requests and answers one line per request. There is no network: everything is text.

## Route table

One route per line: `METHOD PATTERN HANDLER` (exactly three words separated by blanks). `METHOD` is one of `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, or `*` (any method).
Everything from `#` to the end of a line is a comment; lines without words are ignored. Lines are numbered from 1 (comments and blank lines count).

A **handler** is 1 to 24 characters: a lower-case ASCII letter, then lower-case letters, digits or `_`.

A **pattern** starts with `/`. The pattern `/` alone is the root. Otherwise it is segments separated by single `/`, with no empty segment and **no trailing slash**. A segment is:

* a *literal*: one or more of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -`;
* a *parameter* `:name`: matches any one non-empty path segment and captures it; `:name<type>` matches only segments of that type, with the types `hex`, `int`. `name` is 1 to 16 characters, a lower-case letter then lower-case letters, digits or `_`, and a name may occur only once in a pattern;
* the types: `hex`: ASCII hex digits, either case; `int`: 1 to 9 ASCII digits;

A line with the wrong number of words is `bad directive`; otherwise an unknown method is `bad method`, an invalid pattern `bad pattern`, an invalid handler `bad handler` (checked in that order). The first bad line makes the whole result `error: table line N: REASON`.

## Requests

Each non-blank line is `METHOD PATH` (exactly two words): the method is one or more upper-case ASCII letters (any such word is allowed, not only the six above). Lines starting with `#` (after optional blanks) and blank lines produce no output. A request line that does not have the right shape gets the answer `400`.

The **path** is the word after the method with everything from the first `?` removed (the query string is ignored). It must start with `/`, otherwise `400`. The root path is `/`. For any other path the text after the first `/` is split at every `/` into segments. An empty segment *inside* the path (`//`) is `400`. A path with a trailing `/` ends with one empty segment: with the **strict** slash policy it stays, and since no pattern segment can match an empty segment `/a/` is just a path that matches nothing (`404` unless the 400 rules above apply); 

## Matching

A route's pattern **matches** a path if the path has exactly as many segments as the pattern (a wildcard takes all the rest, at least one), and every pattern segment accepts its path segment: literals must be equal (case-sensitively), parameters need a non-empty segment of the right type.

A matching route is *eligible* when its method is `*`, equals the request method, or is `GET` while the request method is `HEAD`. If several routes are eligible, the best one wins: compare their patterns segment by segment from the left, ranking literal > typed parameter > parameter (a position that exists in only one pattern ranks below any kind); the first difference decides. If the patterns are equally specific, an exact method match beats `*`, which beats `GET`-for-`HEAD`; if still tied, the route written **first** in the table wins.

## Answers

* `200 HANDLER name=value ...`: the winning route's handler followed by its captures in the order of the pattern (`name=value`, separated by single blanks; no captures, nothing more).
* `405 allow=M1,M2,...`: no route is eligible but at least one route's pattern matches the path. The methods are collected from those routes (a `*` route contributes all six methods, a `GET` route contributes `GET` and `HEAD`), without duplicates, in the order `GET,HEAD,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE`.
* `404`: no route's pattern matches the path.
* `400`: malformed request (see above).

The result is the answers joined by `\n` (no trailing newline); with no requests it is the empty text.

## Interface

Implement this function in `lib/router.rb` (module `Router`):

```
Router.route(table, requests)
```

* `table`: the route table text
* `requests`: the requests, one per line
* returns one answer line per request (or an `error: table line ...` text).

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Table:

```
HEAD /:id<hex> user
DELETE /:slug<hex>/api files
GET / user
GET /status user
```

Requests:

```
PUT /ff
POST /ff/extra
DELETE /status
HEAD /
OPTIONS /status/
```

Answers:

```
405 allow=HEAD
404
405 allow=GET,HEAD
200 user
404
```

Table:

```
GET /files/:key/api show_item
GET /files/:key search
GET /:id list_items
GET /:rest<hex>/:slug<hex>/orders health
* /v1 create_item
```

Requests:

```
DELETE /ff/ff/orders
HEAD /files/x_y/api
OPTIONS /ff/ff/orders/
PUT /v1
OPTIONS /files/x_y
PATCH /files/x_y/api/
```

Answers:

```
405 allow=GET,HEAD
200 show_item key=x_y
404
200 create_item
405 allow=GET,HEAD
404
```

Table:

```
GET /v2 show_item
* /:slug health
GET /:id<int>/:id1/api about
* /:key<hex>/docs/:name<hex> feed
```

Requests:

```
HEAD /zzz/v2
DELETE /ff/docs/ff
GET /5905/x_y/api
GET /5905/x_y/api/extra
DELETE /x_y?x=1&y=%20
```

Answers:

```
404
200 feed key=ff name=ff
200 about id=5905 id1=x_y
404
200 health slug=x_y
```

# Router for the lighthouse status page

This library decides which handler serves a request for the lighthouse status page. `route(table, requests)` reads a *route table* and a list of requests and answers one line per request. There is no network: everything is text.

## Route table

One route per line: `METHOD PATTERN HANDLER` (exactly three words separated by blanks). `METHOD` is one of `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, or `*` (any method).
Everything from `#` to the end of a line is a comment; lines without words are ignored. Lines are numbered from 1 (comments and blank lines count).

A **handler** is 1 to 24 characters: a lower-case ASCII letter, then lower-case letters, digits or `_`.

A **pattern** starts with `/`. The pattern `/` alone is the root. Otherwise it is segments separated by single `/`, with no empty segment and **no trailing slash**. A segment is:

* a *literal*: one or more of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -`;
* a *parameter* `:name`: matches any one non-empty path segment and captures it; `:name<type>` matches only segments of that type, with the types `hex`, `alpha`. `name` is 1 to 16 characters, a lower-case letter then lower-case letters, digits or `_`, and a name may occur only once in a pattern;
* the types: `hex`: ASCII hex digits, either case; `alpha`: ASCII letters, either case;

A line with the wrong number of words is `bad directive`; otherwise an unknown method is `bad method`, an invalid pattern `bad pattern`, an invalid handler `bad handler` (checked in that order). The first bad line makes the whole result `error: table line N: REASON`.

## Requests

Each non-blank line is `METHOD PATH` (exactly two words): the method is one or more upper-case ASCII letters (any such word is allowed, not only the six above). Lines starting with `#` (after optional blanks) and blank lines produce no output. A request line that does not have the right shape gets the answer `400`.

The **path** is the word after the method with everything from the first `?` removed (the query string is ignored). It must start with `/`, otherwise `400`. The root path is `/`. For any other path the text after the first `/` is split at every `/` into segments. An empty segment *inside* the path (`//`) is `400`. A path with a trailing `/` ends with one empty segment: with the **strict** slash policy it stays, and since no pattern segment can match an empty segment `/a/` is just a path that matches nothing (`404` unless the 400 rules above apply); 

## Matching

A route's pattern **matches** a path if the path has exactly as many segments as the pattern (a wildcard takes all the rest, at least one), and every pattern segment accepts its path segment: literals must be equal (case-sensitively), parameters need a non-empty segment of the right type.

A matching route is *eligible* when its method is `*`, equals the request method, or is `GET` while the request method is `HEAD`. If several routes are eligible, the best one wins: compare their patterns segment by segment from the left, ranking literal > typed parameter > parameter (a position that exists in only one pattern ranks below any kind); the first difference decides. If the patterns are equally specific, an exact method match beats `*`, which beats `GET`-for-`HEAD`; if still tied, the route written **first** in the table wins.

## Answers

* `200 HANDLER name=value ...`: the winning route's handler followed by its captures in the order of the pattern (`name=value`, separated by single blanks; no captures, nothing more).
* `405 allow=M1,M2,...`: no route is eligible but at least one route's pattern matches the path. The methods are collected from those routes (a `*` route contributes all six methods, a `GET` route contributes `GET` and `HEAD`), without duplicates, in the order `GET,HEAD,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE`.
* `404`: no route's pattern matches the path.
* `400`: malformed request (see above).

The result is the answers joined by `\n` (no trailing newline); with no requests it is the empty text.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/router.js`:

```
function route(table, requests)  // returns a string; exported with module.exports
```

* `table`: the route table text
* `requests`: the requests, one per line
* returns one answer line per request (or an `error: table line ...` text).

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Table:

```
* /:n<hex>/items/:name home
* /files/docs about
* /files/orders/:n health
DELETE /:key list_items
```

Requests:

GET /A0b1/items/Q

OPTIONS /zzz/files/orders/42

start.README.md:
# Router for the tide-clock backend

This library decides which handler serves a request for the tide-clock backend. `route(table, requests)` reads a *route table* and a list of requests and answers one line per request. There is no network: everything is text.

## Route table

One route per line: `METHOD PATTERN HANDLER` (exactly three words separated by blanks). `METHOD` is one of `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, or `*` (any method).
Everything from `#` to the end of a line is a comment; lines without words are ignored. Lines are numbered from 1 (comments and blank lines count).

A **handler** is 1 to 24 characters: a lower-case ASCII letter, then lower-case letters, digits or `_`.

A **pattern** starts with `/`. The pattern `/` alone is the root. Otherwise it is segments separated by single `/`, with no empty segment and **no trailing slash**. A segment is:

* a *literal*: one or more of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -`;
* a *parameter* `:name`: matches any one non-empty path segment and captures it; `:name<type>` matches only segments of that type, with the types `slug`, `int`, `alpha`. `name` is 1 to 16 characters, a lower-case letter then lower-case letters, digits or `_`, and a name may occur only once in a pattern;
* the types: `slug`: lower-case letters and digits in groups separated by single `-` (no leading, trailing or double `-`); `int`: 1 to 9 ASCII digits; `alpha`: ASCII letters, either case;
* a *wildcard* `*name` (same naming rules, and the name must differ from the other names), allowed only as the **last** segment: it matches **one or more** remaining segments and captures them joined with `/`.

A line with the wrong number of words is `bad directive`; otherwise an unknown method is `bad method`, an invalid pattern `bad pattern`, an invalid handler `bad handler` (checked in that order). The first bad line makes the whole result `error: table line N: REASON`.

## Requests

Each non-blank line is `METHOD PATH` (exactly two words): the method is one or more upper-case ASCII letters (any such word is allowed, not only the six above). Lines starting with `#` (after optional blanks) and blank lines produce no output. A request line that does not have the right shape gets the answer `400`.

The **path** is the word after the method with everything from the first `?` removed (the query string is ignored). It must start with `/`, otherwise `400`. The root path is `/`. For any other path the text after the first `/` is split at every `/` into segments. An empty segment *inside* the path (`//`) is `400`. A path with a trailing `/` ends with one empty segment: with the **strict** slash policy it stays, and since no pattern segment can match an empty segment `/a/` is just a path that matches nothing (`404` unless the 400 rules above apply); 

**Percent-encoding.** After splitting, every segment is decoded: `%XX` (two hex digits, either case) stands for the character with that code. A `%` not followed by two hex digits, or a decoded character outside the printable ASCII range `0x20`-`0x7E` (so `%00`, `%1F`, `%7F` and every byte from `%80` up are rejected), makes the request `400`. `+` is an ordinary character. A decoded `/` (`%2F`) does **not** separate segments. Matching, typing and the captured values all use the decoded text.

## Matching

A route's pattern **matches** a path if the path has exactly as many segments as the pattern (a wildcard takes all the rest, at least one), and every pattern segment accepts its path segment: literals must be equal (case-sensitively), parameters need a non-empty segment of the right type.

A matching route is *eligible* when its method is `*`, equals the request method, or is `GET` while the request method is `HEAD`. If several routes are eligible, the best one wins: compare their patterns segment by segment from the left, ranking literal > typed parameter > parameter > wildcard (a position that exists in only one pattern ranks below any kind); the first difference decides. If the patterns are equally specific, an exact method match beats `*`, which beats `GET`-for-`HEAD`; if still tied, the route written **first** in the table wins.

## Answers

* `200 HANDLER name=value ...`: the winning route's handler followed by its captures in the order of the pattern (`name=value`, separated by single blanks; no captures, nothing more).
* `405 allow=M1,M2,...`: no route is eligible but at least one route's pattern matches the path. The methods are collected from those routes (a `*` route contributes all six methods, a `GET` route contributes `GET` and `HEAD`), without duplicates, in the order `GET,HEAD,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE`.
* `404`: no route's pattern matches the path.
* `400`: malformed request (see above).

The result is the answers joined by `\n` (no trailing newline); with no requests it is the empty text.

## Interface

Implement this function in `router.go` (package `router`, module `example.com/router`):

```
func Route(table, requests string) string
```

* `table`: the route table text
* `requests`: the requests, one per line
* returns one answer line per request (or an `error: table line ...` text).

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Table:

```
GET / user
GET /v2/status search
PATCH /tags/v1/*tail admin_panel
DELETE /:n<slug> search
```

Requests:

```
DELETE /tags/v1/a/b2/
PATCH /tags/v1/a/b2
PUT /abc
DELETE /tags/v1/a/b2
PATCH /
```

Answers:

```
405 allow=PATCH
200 admin_panel tail=a/b2
405 allow=DELETE
405 allow=PATCH
405 allow=GET,HEAD
```

Table:

```
GET /:id<alpha>/:name<alpha>/status feed
DELETE /api report
PATCH /:id<int> show_item
HEAD /items files
DELETE /:rest/:rest1<int> home
```

Requests:

```
DELETE /items?x=1&y=%20
GET /abc/6891
PATCH /api
GET /zzz/api
GET /3549
PATCH /abc/6891
```

Answers:

```
405 allow=HEAD
405 allow=DELETE
405 allow=DELETE
404
405 allow=PATCH
405 allow=DELETE
```

Table:

```
DELETE / list_items
PUT /:rest/:id create_item
POST /:id<int> search
HEAD /docs/:rest home
```

Requests:

```
OPTIONS /3902
GET /docs/x_y
POST /docs/x_y
GET /zzz/
PATCH /
```

Answers:

```
405 allow=POST
405 allow=HEAD,PUT
405 allow=HEAD,PUT
404
405 allow=DELETE
```

start.README.md:
# Router for the lighthouse status page

This library decides which handler serves a request for the lighthouse status page. `route(table, requests)` reads a *route table* and a list of requests and answers one line per request. There is no network: everything is text.

## Route table

One route per line: `METHOD PATTERN HANDLER` (exactly three words separated by blanks). `METHOD` is one of `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, or `*` (any method).
Everything from `#` to the end of a line is a comment; lines without words are ignored. Lines are numbered from 1 (comments and blank lines count).

A **handler** is 1 to 24 characters: a lower-case ASCII letter, then lower-case letters, digits or `_`.

A **pattern** starts with `/`. The pattern `/` alone is the root. Otherwise it is segments separated by single `/`, with no empty segment and **no trailing slash**. A segment is:

* a *literal*: one or more of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -`;
* a *parameter* `:name`: matches any one non-empty path segment and captures it; `:name<type>` matches only segments of that type, with the types `int`, `slug`. `name` is 1 to 16 characters, a lower-case letter then lower-case letters, digits or `_`, and a name may occur only once in a pattern;
* the types: `int`: 1 to 9 ASCII digits; `slug`: lower-case letters and digits in groups separated by single `-` (no leading, trailing or double `-`);
* a *wildcard* `*name` (same naming rules, and the name must differ from the other names), allowed only as the **last** segment: it matches **one or more** remaining segments and captures them joined with `/`.

A line with the wrong number of words is `bad directive`; otherwise an unknown method is `bad method`, an invalid pattern `bad pattern`, an invalid handler `bad handler` (checked in that order). The first bad line makes the whole result `error: table line N: REASON`.

## Requests

Each non-blank line is `METHOD PATH` (exactly two words): the method is one or more upper-case ASCII letters (any such word is allowed, not only the six above). Lines starting with `#` (after optional blanks) and blank lines produce no output. A request line that does not have the right shape gets the answer `400`.

The **path** is the word after the method with everything from the first `?` removed (the query string is ignored). It must start with `/`, otherwise `400`. The root path is `/`. For any other path the text after the first `/` is split at every `/` into segments. An empty segment *inside* the path (`//`) is `400`. A path with a trailing `/` ends with one empty segment: with the **lenient** slash policy that one trailing slash is simply dropped before matching (so `/a/` is `/a`, but `/a//` is `400`, and `//` is `400`); 

**Percent-encoding.** After splitting, every segment is decoded: `%XX` (two hex digits, either case) stands for the character with that code. A `%` not followed by two hex digits, or a decoded character outside the printable ASCII range `0x20`-`0x7E` (so `%00`, `%1F`, `%7F` and every byte from `%80` up are rejected), makes the request `400`. `+` is an ordinary character. A decoded `/` (`%2F`) does **not** separate segments. Matching, typing and the captured values all use the decoded text.

## Matching

A route's pattern **matches** a path if the path has exactly as many segments as the pattern (a wildcard takes all the rest, at least one), and every pattern segment accepts its path segment: literals must be equal (case-sensitively), parameters need a non-empty segment of the right type.

A matching route is *eligible* when its method is `*`, equals the request method, or is `GET` while the request method is `HEAD`. If several routes are eligible, the best one wins: compare their patterns segment by segment from the left, ranking literal > typed parameter > parameter > wildcard (a position that exists in only one pattern ranks below any kind); the first difference decides. If the patterns are equally specific, an exact method match beats `*`, which beats `GET`-for-`HEAD`; if still tied, the route written **first** in the table wins.

## Answers

* `200 HANDLER name=value ...`: the winning route's handler followed by its captures in the order of the pattern (`name=value`, separated by single blanks; no captures, nothing more).
* `405 allow=M1,M2,...`: no route is eligible but at least one route's pattern matches the path. The methods are collected from those routes (a `*` route contributes all six methods, a `GET` route contributes `GET` and `HEAD`), without duplicates, in the order `GET,HEAD,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE`.
* `404`: no route's pattern matches the path.
* `400`: malformed request (see above).

The result is the answers joined by `\n` (no trailing newline); with no requests it is the empty text.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/Router.java` (class `Router`, default package):

```
public static String route(String table, String requests)
```

* `table`: the route table text
* `requests`: the requests, one per line
* returns one answer line per request (or an `error: table line ...` text).

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Table:

```
PATCH /files/docs/:rest show_item
PATCH /files about
POST /:id<int>/status health
* /:id<int> docs
```

Requests:

```
DELETE /3499
DELETE /9611/status
OPTIONS /9611/status
PATCH /3499
OPTIONS /3499
```

Answers:

```
200 docs id=3499
405 allow=POST
405 allow=POST
200 docs id=3499
200 docs id=3499
```

Table:

```
POST /v1 edit_item
HEAD /:n/:key<int>/docs search
PATCH / report
PATCH /:rest/:rest1<slug> about
DELETE /tags/:key<int> feed
```

Requests:

```
OPTIONS /x_y/3586/docs?x=1&y=%20
OPTIONS /x_y/abc?x=1&y=%20
OPTIONS /x_y/3586/docs/
HEAD /zzz/
POST /tags/458
PATCH /x_y/3586/docs
```

Answers:

```
405 allow=HEAD
405 allow=PATCH
405 allow=HEAD
404
405 allow=PATCH,DELETE
405 allow=HEAD
```

Table:

```
PUT /:id about
PUT /items/v2/*tail create_item
DELETE /tags/users/files/*tail edit_item
* /api/:name<slug> about
```

Requests:

```
POST /api/x1-y2?x=1&y=%20
POST /abc
DELETE /abc
HEAD /abc
DELETE /api/x1-y2/
```

Answers:

```
200 about name=x1-y2
405 allow=PUT
405 allow=PUT
405 allow=PUT
200 about name=x1-y2
```

module Router
  HAS_METHODS = true
  TYPES = ['hex', 'int', 'alpha']
  HAS_WILD = true
  LENIENT = true
  CASEI = false
  HAS_PCT = true
  METHODS = %w[GET HEAD POST PUT PATCH DELETE]
  LOW = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'
  UP = LOW.upcase
  DG = '0123456789'
  HEX = '0123456789abcdefABCDEF'
  RANK = { 'lit' => 3, 'typed' => 2, 'param' => 1, 'wild' => 0 }

  def self.all?(s, set)
    s.each_char.all? { |c| set.include?(c) }
  end

  def self.ident?(s, max)
    s.length >= 1 && s.length <= max && LOW.include?(s[0]) && all?(s, LOW + DG + '_')
  end

  def self.parse_pattern(p)
    return [] if p == '/'
    return nil if !p.start_with?('/') || p.end_with?('/')
    segs = []
    names = []
    parts = p[1..].split('/', -1)
    parts.each_with_index do |s, i|
      return nil if s.empty?
      if s[0] == ':'
        body = s[1..]
        typ = nil
        if body.include?('<')
          return nil if !body.end_with?('>') || body.count('<') != 1
          inner = body[0...-1]
          body, typ = inner.split('<', 2)
          return nil unless TYPES.include?(typ)
        end
        return nil if !ident?(body, 16) || names.include?(body)
        names << body
        segs << [typ ? 'typed' : 'param', body, typ]
      elsif s[0] == '*'
        nm = s[1..]
        return nil if !HAS_WILD || i != parts.length - 1 || !ident?(nm, 16) || names.include?(nm)
        segs << ['wild', nm, nil]
      else
        return nil unless all?(s, LOW + UP + DG + '._~-')
        segs << ['lit', s, nil]
      end
    end
    segs
  end

  def self.type_ok?(typ, s)
    case typ
    when 'int' then s.length >= 1 && s.length <= 9 && all?(s, DG)
    when 'slug' then !s.empty? && all?(s, LOW + DG + '-') && !s.start_with?('-') && !s.end_with?('-') && !s.include?('--')
    when 'alpha' then !s.empty? && all?(s, LOW + UP)
    else !s.empty? && all?(s, HEX)
    end
  end

  def self.match(segs, path)
    caps = []
    i = 0
    segs.each do |kind, name, typ|
      if kind == 'wild'
        return nil if i >= path.length
        caps << [name, path[i..].join('/')]
        return caps
      end
      return nil if i >= path.length
      s = path[i]
      if kind == 'lit'
        return nil if (CASEI ? s.downcase != name.downcase : s != name)
      else
        return nil if s.empty?
        return nil if kind == 'typed' && !type_ok?(typ, s)
        caps << [name, s]
      end
      i += 1
    end
    i == path.length ? caps : nil
  end

  def self.decode(seg)
    out = +''
    i = 0
    while i < seg.length
      c = seg[i]
      if c == '%'
        h = seg[i + 1, 2]
        return nil if h.nil? || h.length != 2 || !all?(h, HEX)
        c = h.to_i(16).chr
        i += 3
      else
        i += 1
      end
      return nil if c < ' ' || c > '~'
      out << c
    end
    out
  end

  def self.parse_table(text)
    routes = []
    text.split("\n", -1).each_with_index do |raw, i|
      w = raw.split('#', 2)[0].to_s.split
      next if w.empty?
      pre = "error: table line #{i + 1}: "
      return [nil, pre + 'bad directive'] if w.length != (HAS_METHODS ? 3 : 2)
      method = '*'
      if HAS_METHODS
        method = w[0]
        return [nil, pre + 'bad method'] if method != '*' && !METHODS.include?(method)
      end
      segs = parse_pattern(w[-2])
      return [nil, pre + 'bad pattern'] if segs.nil?
      return [nil, pre + 'bad handler'] unless ident?(w[-1], 24)
      routes << [method, segs, w[-1]]
    end
    [routes, nil]
  end

  def self.route(table, requests)
    routes, err = parse_table(table)
    return err if err
    out = []
    requests.split("\n", -1).each do |raw|
      next if raw.sub(/\A[ \t]+/, '').start_with?('#')
      w = raw.split
      next if w.empty?
      if w.length != (HAS_METHODS ? 2 : 1)
        out << '400'
        next
      end
      method = 'GET'
      if HAS_METHODS
        method = w[0]
        unless method.match?(/\A[A-Z]+\z/)
          out << '400'
          next
        end
      end
      path = w[-1].split('?', 2)[0].to_s
      unless path.start_with?('/')
        out << '400'
        next
      end
      body = path[1..]
      if path == '/'
        segs = []
      else
        body = body[0...-1] if LENIENT && body.end_with?('/')
        segs = body.empty? ? [''] : body.split('/', -1)
        bad = segs.length == 1 && segs[0].empty? && body.empty?
        segs[0...-1].each { |s| bad = true if s.empty? }
        if bad
          out << '400'
          next
        end
      end
      if HAS_PCT
        dec = []
        bad = false
        segs.each do |s|
          d = decode(s)
          if d.nil?
            bad = true
            break
          end
          dec << d
        end
        if bad
          out << '400'
          next
        end
        segs = dec
      end
      best = nil
      pathmatch = []
      routes.each do |m, rs, h|
        caps = match(rs, segs)
        next if caps.nil?
        pathmatch << m
        next unless m == '*' || m == method || (method == 'HEAD' && m == 'GET')
        spec = rs.map { |k, _, _| RANK[k] }
        exact = m == method ? 2 : m == '*' ? 1 : 0
        if best.nil?
          best = [spec, exact, h, caps]
          next
        end
        n = [spec.length, best[0].length].max
        cmp = 0
        k = 0
        while k < n && cmp == 0
          a = k < spec.length ? spec[k] : -1
          b = k < best[0].length ? best[0][k] : -1
          cmp = a - b
          k += 1
        end
        cmp = exact - best[1] if cmp == 0
        best = [spec, exact, h, caps] if cmp > 0
      end
      if best
        out << (['200', best[2]] + best[3].map { |k, v| "#{k}=#{v}" }).join(' ')
      elsif !pathmatch.empty?
        allowed = []
        pathmatch.each do |m|
          if m == '*' then allowed.concat(METHODS)
          elsif m == 'GET' then allowed.push('GET', 'HEAD')
          else allowed << m
          end
        end
        out << ('405 allow=' + METHODS.select { |x| allowed.include?(x) }.join(','))
      else
        out << '404'
      end
    end
    out.join("\n")
  end
end

start.README.md:
# Router for a harbour fee service

This library decides which handler serves a request for a harbour fee service. `route(table, requests)` reads a *route table* and a list of requests and answers one line per request. There is no network: everything is text.

## Route table

One route per line: `METHOD PATTERN HANDLER` (exactly three words separated by blanks). `METHOD` is one of `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, or `*` (any method).
Everything from `#` to the end of a line is a comment; lines without words are ignored. Lines are numbered from 1 (comments and blank lines count).

A **handler** is 1 to 24 characters: a lower-case ASCII letter, then lower-case letters, digits or `_`.

A **pattern** starts with `/`. The pattern `/` alone is the root. Otherwise it is segments separated by single `/`, with no empty segment and **no trailing slash**. A segment is:

* a *literal*: one or more of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -`;
* a *parameter* `:name`: matches any one non-empty path segment and captures it; `:name<type>` matches only segments of that type, with the types `hex`, `int`, `alpha`. `name` is 1 to 16 characters, a lower-case letter then lower-case letters, digits or `_`, and a name may occur only once in a pattern;
* the types: `hex`: ASCII hex digits, either case; `int`: 1 to 9 ASCII digits; `alpha`: ASCII letters, either case;
* a *wildcard* `*name` (same naming rules, and the name must differ from the other names), allowed only as the **last** segment: it matches **one or more** remaining segments and captures them joined with `/`.

A line with the wrong number of words is `bad directive`; otherwise an unknown method is `bad method`, an invalid pattern `bad pattern`, an invalid handler `bad handler` (checked in that order). The first bad line makes the whole result `error: table line N: REASON`.

## Requests

Each non-blank line is `METHOD PATH` (exactly two words): the method is one or more upper-case ASCII letters (any such word is allowed, not only the six above). Lines starting with `#` (after optional blanks) and blank lines produce no output. A request line that does not have the right shape gets the answer `400`.

The **path** is the word after the method with everything from the first `?` removed (the query string is ignored). It must start with `/`, otherwise `400`. The root path is `/`. For any other path the text after the first `/` is split at every `/` into segments. An empty segment *inside* the path (`//`) is `400`. A path with a trailing `/` ends with one empty segment: with the **lenient** slash policy that one trailing slash is simply dropped before matching (so `/a/` is `/a`, but `/a//` is `400`, and `//` is `400`); 

**Percent-encoding.** After splitting, every segment is decoded: `%XX` (two hex digits, either case) stands for the character with that code. A `%` not followed by two hex digits, or a decoded character outside the printable ASCII range `0x20`-`0x7E` (so `%00`, `%1F`, `%7F` and every byte from `%80` up are rejected), makes the request `400`. `+` is an ordinary character. A decoded `/` (`%2F`) does **not** separate segments. Matching, typing and the captured values all use the decoded text.

## Matching

A route's pattern **matches** a path if the path has exactly as many segments as the pattern (a wildcard takes all the rest, at least one), and every pattern segment accepts its path segment: literals must be equal (case-sensitively), parameters need a non-empty segment of the right type.

A matching route is *eligible* when its method is `*`, equals the request method, or is `GET` while the request method is `HEAD`. If several routes are eligible, the best one wins: compare their patterns segment by segment from the left, ranking literal > typed parameter > parameter > wildcard (a position that exists in only one pattern ranks below any kind); the first difference decides. If the patterns are equally specific, an exact method match beats `*`, which beats `GET`-for-`HEAD`; if still tied, the route written **first** in the table wins.

## Answers

* `200 HANDLER name=value ...`: the winning route's handler followed by its captures in the order of the pattern (`name=value`, separated by single blanks; no captures, nothing more).
* `405 allow=M1,M2,...`: no route is eligible but at least one route's pattern matches the path. The methods are collected from those routes (a `*` route contributes all six methods, a `GET` route contributes `GET` and `HEAD`), without duplicates, in the order `GET,HEAD,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE`.
* `404`: no route's pattern matches the path.
* `400`: malformed request (see above).

The result is the answers joined by `\n` (no trailing newline); with no requests it is the empty text.

## Interface

Implement this function in `lib/router.rb` (module `Router`):

```
Router.route(table, requests)
```

* `table`: the route table text
* `requests`: the requests, one per line
* returns one answer line per request (or an `error: table line ...` text).

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Table:

```
DELETE /items create_item
DELETE /:slug<int>/*tail report
DELETE /:n<int> home
GET /users/users about
```

Requests:

```
HEAD /497
GET /items
DELETE /497
PATCH /4400/b2/a
PATCH /497
```

Answers:

```
405 allow=DELETE
405 allow=DELETE
200 home n=497
405 allow=DELETE
405 allow=DELETE
```

Table:

```
DELETE /files/:id/:n/*tail feed
PUT /:key/:n edit_item
GET /docs/*tail show_item
GET /status feed
DELETE /:name/tags list_items
```

Requests:

```
PUT /abc/abc
PUT /x_y/tags
HEAD /x_y/tags
DELETE /docs/a
DELETE /files/x_y/Q/b2/b2
DELETE /zzz/docs/a
```

Answers:

```
200 edit_item key=abc n=abc
200 edit_item key=x_y n=tags
405 allow=PUT,DELETE
405 allow=GET,HEAD,PUT
200 feed id=x_y n=Q tail=b2/b2

```

```

Answers:

```

start.README.md:
# Router for the Hollin allotment portal

This library decides which handler serves a request for the Hollin allotment portal. `route(table, requests)` reads a *route table* and a list of requests and answers one line per request. There is no network: everything is text.

## Route table

One route per line: `METHOD PATTERN HANDLER` (exactly three words separated by blanks). `METHOD` is one of `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, or `*` (any method).
Everything from `#` to the end of a line is a comment; lines without words are ignored. Lines are numbered from 1 (comments and blank lines count).

A **handler** is 1 to 24 characters: a lower-case ASCII letter, then lower-case letters, digits or `_`.

A **pattern** starts with `/`. The pattern `/` alone is the root. Otherwise it is segments separated by single `/`, with no empty segment and **no trailing slash**. A segment is:

* a *literal*: one or more of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -`;
* a *parameter* `:name`: matches any one non-empty path segment and captures it; `:name<type>` matches only segments of that type, with the types `slug`, `hex`, `alpha`. `name` is 1 to 16 characters, a lower-case letter then lower-case letters, digits or `_`, and a name may occur only once in a pattern;
* the types: `slug`: lower-case letters and digits in groups separated by single `-` (no leading, trailing or double `-`); `hex`: ASCII hex digits, either case; `alpha`: ASCII letters, either case;

A line with the wrong number of words is `bad directive`; otherwise an unknown method is `bad method`, an invalid pattern `bad pattern`, an invalid handler `bad handler` (checked in that order). The first bad line makes the whole result `error: table line N: REASON`.

## Requests

Each non-blank line is `METHOD PATH` (exactly two words): the method is one or more upper-case ASCII letters (any such word is allowed, not only the six above). Lines starting with `#` (after optional blanks) and blank lines produce no output. A request line that does not have the right shape gets the answer `400`.

The **path** is the word after the method with everything from the first `?` removed (the query string is ignored). It must start with `/`, otherwise `400`. The root path is `/`. For any other path the text after the first `/` is split at every `/` into segments. An empty segment *inside* the path (`//`) is `400`. A path with a trailing `/` ends with one empty segment: with the **strict** slash policy it stays, and since no pattern segment can match an empty segment `/a/` is just a path that matches nothing (`404` unless the 400 rules above apply); 

## Matching

A route's pattern **matches** a path if the path has exactly as many segments as the pattern (a wildcard takes all the rest, at least one), and every pattern segment accepts its path segment: literals must be equal (case-sensitively), parameters need a non-empty segment of the right type.

A matching route is *eligible* when its method is `*`, equals the request method, or is `GET` while the request method is `HEAD`. If several routes are eligible, the best one wins: compare their patterns segment by segment from the left, ranking literal > typed parameter > parameter (a position that exists in only one pattern ranks below any kind); the first difference decides. If the patterns are equally specific, an exact method match beats `*`, which beats `GET`-for-`HEAD`; if still tied, the route written **first** in the table wins.

## Answers

* `200 HANDLER name=value ...`: the winning route's handler followed by its captures in the order of the pattern (`name=value`, separated by single blanks; no captures, nothing more).
* `405 allow=M1,M2,...`: no route is eligible but at least one route's pattern matches the path. The methods are collected from those routes (a `*` route contributes all six methods, a `GET` route contributes `GET` and `HEAD`), without duplicates, in the order `GET,HEAD,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE`.
* `404`: no route's pattern matches the path.
* `400`: malformed request (see above).

The result is the answers joined by `\n` (no trailing newline); with no requests it is the empty text.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/router.js`:

```
function route(table, requests)  // returns a string; exported with module.exports
```

* `table`: the route table text
* `requests`: the requests, one per line
* returns one answer line per request (or an `error: table line ...` text).

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Table:

```
PUT /v2/:rest admin_panel
PUT /v2/v1/tags health
* /:name/items/docs feed
PUT /:rest<slug>/items create_item
```

Requests:

```
OPTIONS /v2/v1/tags
PUT /x1-y2/items/
PUT /v2/v1/tags
POST /x_y/items/docs/extra
GET /x1-y2/items?x=1&y=%20
```

Answers:

```
405 allow=PUT
404
200 health
404
405 allow=PUT
```

Table:

```
GET /:rest<hex> feed
HEAD /:slug<alpha>/:slug1/:n<slug> health
POST /:name/:rest admin_panel
POST /status/:id<alpha>/:key<slug> health
POST /:n/:key/:n2 search
```

Requests:

```
POST /abc/Q/
OPTIONS /Abc/42/x1-y2/
GET /ff
GET /42/42/Q/
HEAD /ff
OPTIONS /abc/Q
```

Answers:

```
404
404
200 feed rest=ff
404
200 feed rest=ff
405 allow=POST
```

Table:

```
POST /v2/:name<slug>/status health
PUT /api/docs report
PUT /api/:n list_items
* /:id<hex> feed
```

Requests:

```
PATCH /v2/abc/status
HEAD /v2/abc/status
PATCH /ff/
GET /api/abc
DELETE /api/docs
```

Answers:

```
405 allow=POST
405 allow=POST
404
405 allow=PUT
405 allow=PUT
```

start.README.md:
# Router for the Saltmarsh library service

This library decides which handler serves a request for the Saltmarsh library service. `route(table, requests)` reads a *route table* and a list of requests and answers one line per request. There is no network: everything is text.

## Route table

One route per line: `METHOD PATTERN HANDLER` (exactly three words separated by blanks). `METHOD` is one of `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, or `*` (any method).
Everything from `#` to the end of a line is a comment; lines without words are ignored. Lines are numbered from 1 (comments and blank lines count).

A **handler** is 1 to 24 characters: a lower-case ASCII letter, then lower-case letters, digits or `_`.

A **pattern** starts with `/`. The pattern `/` alone is the root. Otherwise it is segments separated by single `/`, with no empty segment and **no trailing slash**. A segment is:

* a *literal*: one or more of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -`;
* a *parameter* `:name`: matches any one non-empty path segment and captures it; `:name<type>` matches only segments of that type, with the types `hex`, `alpha`. `name` is 1 to 16 characters, a lower-case letter then lower-case letters, digits or `_`, and a name may occur only once in a pattern;
* the types: `hex`: ASCII hex digits, either case; `alpha`: ASCII letters, either case;
* a *wildcard* `*name` (same naming rules, and the name must differ from the other names), allowed only as the **last** segment: it matches **one or more** remaining segments and captures them joined with `/`.

A line with the wrong number of words is `bad directive`; otherwise an unknown method is `bad method`, an invalid pattern `bad pattern`, an invalid handler `bad handler` (checked in that order). The first bad line makes the whole result `error: table line N: REASON`.

## Requests

Each non-blank line is `METHOD PATH` (exactly two words): the method is one or more upper-case ASCII letters (any such word is allowed, not only the six above). Lines starting with `#` (after optional blanks) and blank lines produce no output. A request line that does not have the right shape gets the answer `400`.

The **path** is the word after the method with everything from the first `?` removed (the query string is ignored). It must start with `/`, otherwise `400`. The root path is `/`. For any other path the text after the first `/` is split at every `/` into segments. An empty segment *inside* the path (`//`) is `400`. A path with a trailing `/` ends with one empty segment: with the **lenient** slash policy that one trailing slash is simply dropped before matching (so `/a/` is `/a`, but `/a//` is `400`, and `//` is `400`); 

**Percent-encoding.** After splitting, every segment is decoded: `%XX` (two hex digits, either case) stands for the character with that code. A `%` not followed by two hex digits, or a decoded character outside the printable ASCII range `0x20`-`0x7E` (so `%00`, `%1F`, `%7F` and every byte from `%80` up are rejected), makes the request `400`. `+` is an ordinary character. A decoded `/` (`%2F`) does **not** separate segments. Matching, typing and the captured values all use the decoded text.

## Matching

A route's pattern **matches** a path if the path has exactly as many segments as the pattern (a wildcard takes all the rest, at least one), and every pattern segment accepts its path segment: literals must be equal ignoring ASCII case (a request for `/Members` matches the literal `members`; captured values keep their case), parameters need a non-empty segment of the right type.

A matching route is *eligible* when its method is `*`, equals the request method, or is `GET` while the request method is `HEAD`. If several routes are eligible, the best one wins: compare their patterns segment by segment from the left, ranking literal > typed parameter > parameter > wildcard (a position that exists in only one pattern ranks below any kind); the first difference decides. If the patterns are equally specific, an exact method match beats `*`, which beats `GET`-for-`HEAD`; if still tied, the route written **first** in the table wins.

## Answers

* `200 HANDLER name=value ...`: the winning route's handler followed by its captures in the order of the pattern (`name=value`, separated by single blanks; no captures, nothing more).
* `405 allow=M1,M2,...`: no route is eligible but at least one route's pattern matches the path. The methods are collected from those routes (a `*` route contributes all six methods, a `GET` route contributes `GET` and `HEAD`), without duplicates, in the order `GET,HEAD,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE`.
* `404`: no route's pattern matches the path.
* `400`: malformed request (see above).

The result is the answers joined by `\n` (no trailing newline); with no requests it is the empty text.

## Interface

Implement this function in `router.go` (package `router`, module `example.com/router`):

```
func Route(table, requests string) string
```

* `table`: the route table text
* `requests`: the requests, one per line
* returns one answer line per request (or an `error: table line ...` text).

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Table:

```
GET /:n feed
GET /users/docs/docs user
GET /v2/docs/files admin_panel
GET / search
```

Requests:

```
HEAD /users/docs/docs?x=1&y=%20
PATCH /zzz/users/docs/docs
GET /v2/docs/files
OPTIONS //
GET /
```

Answers:

```
200 user
404
200 admin_panel
400
200 search
```

Table:

```
DELETE /v2/*tail docs
GET /orders/:rest<hex> docs
HEAD /:slug/*tail create_item
GET /docs/:id/:slug<hex> docs
POST /:name<hex> health
```

Requests:

```
PATCH /orders/A0b1
DELETE /v2/c.d/b2?x=1&y=%20
HEAD /docs/42/A0b1
PUT /docs/42/A0b1/
GET /orders/A0b1
GET /docs/42/A0b1/
```

Answers:

```
405 allow=GET,HEAD
200 docs tail=c.d/b2
200 docs id=42 slug=A0b1
405 allow=GET,HEAD
200 docs rest=A0b1
200 docs id=42 slug=A0b1
```

Table:

```
PATCH /:name<alpha>/users/:slug<alpha> user
* /v2/items health
* / health
POST /api feed
```

Requests:

```
GET /
DELETE /api
GET /v2/items/
GET /
PATCH /v2/items/
```

Answers:

```
200 health
405 allow=POST
200 health
200 health
200 health
```

start.README.md:
# Router for the lighthouse status page

This library decides which handler serves a request for the lighthouse status page. `route(table, requests)` reads a *route table* and a list of requests and answers one line per request. There is no network: everything is text.

## Route table

One route per line: `PATTERN HANDLER` (exactly two words separated by blanks). Routes answer every request; requests carry no method.
Everything from `#` to the end of a line is a comment; lines without words are ignored. Lines are numbered from 1 (comments and blank lines count).

A **handler** is 1 to 24 characters: a lower-case ASCII letter, then lower-case letters, digits or `_`.

A **pattern** starts with `/`. The pattern `/` alone is the root. Otherwise it is segments separated by single `/`, with no empty segment and **no trailing slash**. A segment is:

* a *literal*: one or more of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -`;
* a *parameter* `:name`: matches any one non-empty path segment and captures it. `name` is 1 to 16 characters, a lower-case letter then lower-case letters, digits or `_`, and a name may occur only once in a pattern;

A line with the wrong number of words is `bad directive`; otherwise an invalid pattern `bad pattern`, an invalid handler `bad handler` (checked in that order). The first bad line makes the whole result `error: table line N: REASON`.

## Requests

Each non-blank line is just a `PATH` (exactly one word). Lines starting with `#` (after optional blanks) and blank lines produce no output. A request line that does not have the right shape gets the answer `400`.

The **path** is the word after the method with everything from the first `?` removed (the query string is ignored). It must start with `/`, otherwise `400`. The root path is `/`. For any other path the text after the first `/` is split at every `/` into segments. An empty segment *inside* the path (`//`) is `400`. A path with a trailing `/` ends with one empty segment: with the **strict** slash policy it stays, and since no pattern segment can match an empty segment `/a/` is just a path that matches nothing (`404` unless the 400 rules above apply); 

## Matching

A route's pattern **matches** a path if the path has exactly as many segments as the pattern (a wildcard takes all the rest, at least one), and every pattern segment accepts its path segment: literals must be equal (case-sensitively), parameters need a non-empty segment.

If several routes match, the best one wins: compare their patterns segment by segment from the left, ranking literal > parameter (a position that exists in only one pattern ranks below any kind); the first difference decides; if still tied the route written **first** wins.

## Answers

* `200 HANDLER name=value ...`: the winning route's handler followed by its captures in the order of the pattern (`name=value`, separated by single blanks; no captures, nothing more).
* `404`: no route's pattern matches the path.
* `400`: malformed request (see above).

The result is the answers joined by `\n` (no trailing newline); with no requests it is the empty text.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/Router.java` (class `Router`, default package):

```
public static String route(String table, String requests)
```

* `table`: the route table text
* `requests`: the requests, one per line
* returns one answer line per request (or an `error: table line ...` text).

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Table:

```
/:rest/:id/orders home
/:name/docs/:slug user
/:key show_item
/:key create_item
```

Requests:

```
/Q
/Q
/abc/docs/abc?x=1&y=%20
/Q?x=1&y=%20
/Q
```

Answers:

```
200 show_item key=Q
200 show_item key=Q
200 user name=abc slug=abc
200 show_item key=Q
200 show_item key=Q
```

Table:

```
/:key/:name/:slug user
/files/files docs
/users/:id/orders edit_item
/ feed
/docs list_items
```

Requests:

```
/
/files/files
/docs
/users/x_y/orders/extra
/zzz/abc/42/abc
/users/x_y/orders
```

Answers:

```
200 feed
200 docs
200 list_items
404
404
200 edit_item id=x_y
```

Table:

```
/:slug/:key/items list_items
/:id/:rest show_item
/:slug list_items
/:n files
```

Requests:

```
/x_y/x_y
/abc/
/x_y/x_y
/abc
/42
```

Answers:

```
200 show_item id=x_y rest=x_y
404
200 show_item id=x_y rest=x_y
200 list_items slug=abc
200 list_items slug=42
```
